subject: Architecture
title: Underground Cities: Building Downward
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Underground Cities: Building Downward.

hook.text: Helsinki has an underground city — swimming pools, hockey rinks, and shopping malls carved into bedrock.

buildup.text: 400 underground facilities serve the city — natural rock insulation keeps temperatures constant year-round.

discovery.text: Montreal's RÉSO connects 20 miles of underground corridors — 500,000 people use it daily to escape winter.

twist.text: Singapore is planning underground science labs, storage, and transportation — saving surface land for housing.

climax.text: Underground construction is earthquake-resistant — tunnels flex with the ground instead of shaking apart.

punchline.text: The future of cities might not be taller buildings. It might be deeper ones.

quiz.question: Why is underground construction earthquake-resistant?
options: Rock absorbs all vibration before it reaches structures
Tunnels flex with the ground instead of shaking apart
Underground buildings have no tall components to topple
